newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk leftist in murder hunt surrenders in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Turk leftist in murder hunt surrenders in Syria.

text.p: A Turkish leftist urban guerrilla wanted for the killing last year of a leading businessman has given himself in to Turkey's embassy in Damascus and been brought back to Istanbul, government officials said on Monday.
An official at the Istanbul governor's office confirmed that Mustafa Duyar, a member of the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front (DHKP-C), was being held in custody in the city.
"At the moment he is in the anti-terror branch of Istanbul police," he told Reuters.

Anatolian news agency quoted Interior Minister Meral Aksener as saying Duyar, 26, turned up at the embassy around two weeks ago and admitted to a part in the killing of businessman Ozdemir Sabanci and two others in a high-profile attack last January 9.
Aksener said the suspect had become disillusioned with his far-left group but added that he was pressured into turning himself in due to surveillance by Turkish security forces.

"You can't say he gave himself up on his own," she said. "This person was being followed, wherever he went he was being followed. In the end he saw there was no other way out and he surrendered to our Damascus embassy," she said.
Aksener and other Turkish officials did not explain why Duyar was in neighbouring Syria and if Syrian authorities had been aware of his presence and transfer to Turkey.
The Turkish press said members of the national intelligence service had travelled to Damascus and brought Duyar to Ankara and then Istanbul where they handed him over to anti-terror police.
He was one of three people wanted for killing Sabanci, the head of the Toyotasa joint venture with Japan and a member of one of the country's top industrial dynasties.
Toyotasa's general manager and a secretary also died in the attack at the company's twin-tower headquarters.
DHKP-C, Turkey's most lethal armed leftist group, claimed responsibility for the killings.
